entries.description: During the broom journey Harry recalls extreme cold while playing Hufflepuff in a storm in his third year.
entries.temporal: Recollection in August 1995 of third-year Quidditch storm
entries.model_notes: Narrated weather memory, without a new pitch layout or numerical temperature. The present broom flight ends in London and is not a Hogwarts access route.

entries.description: A Ministry basement corridor with rough stone walls and bracket-mounted torches is said to resemble the corridor leading to Snape’s dungeon at Hogwarts.
entries.temporal: August 1995 comparison with existing Hogwarts dungeon approach
entries.model_notes: Record the rough stone and torch-bracket comparison. The heavy bolted doors described as here belong to the Ministry corridor and are not imported as Hogwarts door specifications.

entries.description: Harry recalls walking across the vegetable patches to reach the Herbology greenhouses.
entries.temporal: Recollection before September 1995 return to school
entries.model_notes: A remembered everyday approach, not a newly observed journey; establishes vegetable plots along a greenhouse approach without a compass bearing.

entries.description: The barrier between platforms nine and ten admits travellers to platform nine and three-quarters; arrivals emerge through a wrought-iron arch, beside the steam-belching Hogwarts Express.
entries.model_notes: The remote London terminus is included only as the school rail connection.

entries.description: A corridor serves compartments with glass-panelled sliding doors; luggage racks hold trunks and owl cages. The prefect carriage is toward the engine; Harry finds seating in the last carriage after passing five occupied carriages.
entries.model_notes: Transport geometry, without an invented carriage total or exact seat plan.

entries.description: The train travels farther north through open country; carriage lamps come on at night. Harry attempts a distant castle view through a grimy rain-streaked window, but the moonless darkness prevents it.
entries.model_notes: Do not turn the attempted view into a confirmed sightline or locate the railway by compass bearing from the castle.

entries.description: Pine trees line the path down to the lake, their smell reaching the arrival platform. First-years assemble separately under a teacher carrying a lantern.
entries.model_notes: The downward path and pine lining are explicit; no first-year boat journey is narrated here.

entries.description: Students leave the platform through the station, passing a narrow doorway onto the dark rain-washed road outside. Roughly a hundred stagecoaches wait there to take pupils above first year up to the castle.
entries.model_notes: Preserve road-to-station adjacency and uphill destination; no road length given.

entries.location: Station coaches and their draft animals
entries.description: Skeletal black horse-like creatures stand harnessed between the coach shafts. They have dragon-like heads, white pupil-less eyes and large black leathery bat-like wings; vapour issues from their nostrils in the cold station light.
entries.model_notes: Animal clearance and harness placement matter for transport animation. Species name is not supplied in this chapter.

entries.description: Harry and Luna can see the harnessed winged creatures while Ron cannot, even standing directly before one.
entries.model_notes: An observed visibility difference; its cause is not established by this passage.

entries.description: Luna says she has seen the creatures since her first day and that they have always pulled the carriages.
entries.model_notes: Character report, distinct from Harry’s previous assumption that the coaches moved by themselves.

entries.description: Passengers climb into the coach’s dark, musty interior; one coach accommodates Hermione, Ginny, Ron, Luna and Harry.
entries.model_notes: At least five occupants in this instance; upholstery and seating configuration unspecified.

entries.description: The creaking wheeled coaches travel uphill in convoy through the grounds gates, between tall stone pillars topped with winged boars; the vehicles have doors and windows.
entries.model_notes: Connect station road to gated grounds; no count of intervening bends.

entries.description: A towering mass of castle turrets rises against the night sky, with some windows brightly lit above the arrivals. Hagrid’s cabin stands by the Forbidden Forest; Harry looks toward it both from the gate approach and the coach stopping place but sees no light.
entries.model_notes: Cabin darkness is a temporary absence, not proof of abandonment. Preserve attempted viewing positions without assuming unobstructed daytime sightlines.

entries.description: Coaches stop near stone steps leading to the oak front doors. Inside, torches illuminate a flagged stone floor; double doors on the right lead to the Great Hall.
entries.model_notes: Right is relative to entering from the front doors.

entries.description: Four long house tables sit beneath a starless black ceiling matching the sky visible through high windows. Candles float above the tables and translucent ghosts mingle among pupils.
entries.model_notes: September night state; ghost movement is not restricted to physical seats.

entries.location: Great Hall staff table and chair
entries.description: The long staff table runs along the top wall. Dumbledore occupies a high-backed golden chair in its centre; Umbridge sits beside him, and Grubbly-Plank takes Hagrid’s place at the very end.
entries.model_notes: Named seating is this feast’s arrangement; no compass orientation.

entries.description: First-years enter from the Entrance Hall and line up in front of the staff table facing the school. McGonagall sets a stool carrying the patched, darned, frayed Sorting Hat in front of them and removes both after Sorting.
entries.model_notes: Ceremonial movable furniture rather than a permanent obstacle.

entries.description: Food appears on all five long tables, including joints, pies, vegetables, bread, sauces and pumpkin-juice flagons.
entries.model_notes: Five includes the staff table; mechanism not explained here.

entries.description: Nearly Headless Nick says the Sorting Hat lives in Dumbledore’s office.
entries.model_notes: Reported storage location; his idea that it overhears information is speculation.

entries.description: Dumbledore declares the grounds’ Forest out of bounds to students and says magic is forbidden in corridors between lessons.
entries.model_notes: Institutional rules, not demonstrated physical magical barriers.

entries.description: Dumbledore says an extensive list of forbidden things is fastened to the caretaker’s office door.
entries.model_notes: Reported fixture; door location and list dimensions unspecified.

entries.description: Gryffindor first-years approach their prefects through the gap between the Gryffindor and Hufflepuff tables.
entries.model_notes: Establishes adjacency without supplying complete table order.

entries.description: Harry leaves the Great Hall into the crowded Entrance Hall, climbs the marble staircase and takes two concealed shortcuts through upstairs corridors, reaching the end of the corridor to Gryffindor common room.
entries.model_notes: Shortcuts are real but undescribed; do not invent their doors, length or landing floors.

entries.description: At the corridor end, the Fat Lady in a pink satin dress refuses entry without a password. Mimbulus mimbletonia causes her portrait to swing outward like a door, exposing a circular wall opening through which pupils climb.
entries.model_notes: Date the password; circular opening and swinging portrait are distinct components.

entries.description: The cosy circular tower room contains dilapidated squashy armchairs, rickety tables and a crackling fire in a grate. Across the room the twins pin material to a noticeboard; a door leads toward the boys’ dormitories.
entries.model_notes: Dormitories are above the common room according to pupils going up; no precise spiral route is supplied here.

entries.description: Dean and Seamus decorate walls beside their beds with posters and photographs, including a Kenmare Kestrels team poster. Neville places his Mimbulus mimbletonia on his bedside cabinet; Harry has a trunk and bedside table. Ron’s bed is next to Harry’s.
entries.model_notes: Personal decorations and plant belong to the 1995–96 occupancy.

entries.description: Harry anticipates a soft warm four-poster bed above the Hall. The dormitory beds have closable hangings, pillows and covers; Seamus tears his hangings down and repairs them by wand. Moonlight reaches Neville’s cactus, and Ron extinguishes the last candle.
entries.model_notes: Temporary torn curtains are repaired in the same scene; no window size or exact count follows from the moonlight.

entries.description: A recruitment notice for the twins’ paid experiments covers a poster announcing October’s first Hogsmeade weekend; Hermione removes the top notice.
entries.model_notes: Layered removable notices on the common-room board.

entries.description: After climbing out of the portrait hole, the friends descend a staircase lined with talking portraits of old witches and wizards, then reach the foot of the marble staircase in the Entrance Hall and enter the Great Hall.
entries.model_notes: Sequence does not establish that the portrait-lined flight is the marble stair itself.

entries.location: Great Hall breakfast weather and owl entry
entries.description: The enchanted ceiling is rain-cloud grey; pupils sit on benches. Hundreds of owls enter through upper windows to deliver post, scattering rainwater over breakfast tables.
entries.model_notes: Upper windows are functioning owl entrances; seasonal wet state.

entries.description: Binns leaves his classroom by drifting through its blackboard.
entries.model_notes: Confirms a blackboard and nonphysical ghost traversal; not a passage for living pupils.

entries.description: After leaving History of Magic, the friends go into a damp courtyard, choosing a secluded corner below a heavily dripping balcony in misty September drizzle.
entries.model_notes: Courtyard has a corner and overhead balcony; adjacency to classroom is a travelled route without a stated intervening distance.

entries.description: At the lesson bell they travel down to Snape’s dungeon and queue outside the classroom door before entering.
entries.model_notes: Descending route from the courtyard; floors unspecified.

entries.description: Harry, Ron and Hermione use their usual table at the back, with Hermione to Harry’s left; Slytherins sit at the front. Snape has a desk, a blackboard and an ingredient store cupboard with a door that he opens by wand.
entries.model_notes: Seating is observed for this class; cupboard is not assumed to be Snape’s private store.

entries.description: Cauldrons simmer over controllable flames. Grey steam, green sparks and silver mist rise from different mixtures; multi-coloured vapour makes the blackboard difficult to read. Goyle’s sample flagon reportedly shatters and sets his clothes alight.
entries.model_notes: Fire incident is Hermione’s report within an otherwise observed lesson; avoid permanent scorch damage not stated.

entries.location: Great Hall storm and route upward
entries.description: After Potions Harry lunches in the Hall beneath a darker grey ceiling with rain lashing high windows; he then climbs the marble staircase.
entries.model_notes: Repeat weather description and concrete travel segment.

entries.description: A large portrait of Sir Cadogan occupies a landing on Harry’s upward route; its knight tries entering the neighbouring portrait but is repelled by the large wolfhound inhabiting it.
entries.model_notes: Picture-to-picture character movement does not establish a human doorway.

entries.description: Harry waits beneath a trapdoor at the top of North Tower, then climbs the silver ladder into Trelawney’s classroom; the class descends that ladder afterward.
entries.model_notes: Top-of-tower access, distinct from unspecified earlier stairs.

entries.description: Spindly small tables carry battered leather-bound books. Scarves cover the lamps, and a low sickly-scented fire supplies little light. Tables, chairs and overstuffed pouffes impede direct paths across the room.
entries.model_notes: Retain dim shadowed seating and crowded circulation.

entries.description: Umbridge sits behind the teacher’s desk; she writes magically on a blackboard. Pupils have seats including stools and a chair Harry kicks aside; their work uses quills, ink and parchment.
entries.model_notes: Specific stool and chair observations do not establish uniform classroom seating.

entries.description: Harry exits Defence, follows a corridor, turns a corner and runs down the nearest staircase with a banister. McGonagall emerges from an office door to his left.
entries.model_notes: Observed sequence includes an evasive detour from Peeves; not necessarily the shortest route or proof of one-floor separation.

entries.description: Peeves drops two inkwells in the corridor near Defence, smashing them and splattering ink on the walls.
entries.model_notes: Temporary local mess; no repair described.

entries.description: The study door closes automatically behind Harry. McGonagall sits at a desk piled with papers and a tartan biscuit tin, with a visitor’s chair opposite. Student movement can be heard overhead and around the office when the bell rings.
entries.model_notes: Do not infer a precise floor from overhead footfalls; automatic closing is observed without its mechanism.

entries.description: Leaving dinner the friends reach a first-floor landing, then traverse windowed corridors toward Gryffindor Tower. A rain-washed window at the turn into the Fat Lady’s corridor gives Harry a view toward Hagrid’s still-unlit cabin.
entries.model_notes: Do not assign the Fat Lady corridor to the first floor; further travel intervenes.

entries.description: Hermione recalls Harry arriving in the middle of the lawn carrying Cedric’s body after the maze task.
entries.model_notes: Reported retrospective placement complements the earlier return account; no lawn coordinates.

entries.description: The friends occupy three favourite armchairs by the fire; Hermione’s chair has holes leaking stuffing. Bags are stored in a corner, and a small table stands by the fireplace.
entries.model_notes: Worn upholstered furniture, not immaculate replacements.

entries.description: A door leads to the girls’ dormitories. Harry passes the boys’ dormitory door to a stone spiral staircase; later he climbs up from late common-room study to bed.
entries.model_notes: Doors and separate approaches confirmed; no new floor count.

entries.description: Hermione places woollen hats under rubbish on the table by the fireplace; Ron uncovers the first pair. By Friday more hats are hidden throughout the room, and a Butterbeer celebration occupies it.
entries.model_notes: Temporary props; disappearance alone does not prove elves were freed.

entries.description: Flitwick perches on a pile of books to see over his desk during Charms.
entries.model_notes: Scale aid for the teacher; pile height unspecified.

entries.location: Sloping lawn and outdoor creature classroom
entries.description: The class walks down the sloping lawn to Hagrid’s cabin at the Forest edge. Grubbly-Plank waits about ten yards from the front door behind a long trestle table of Bowtruckles and woodlice; students work sitting or crouching on the grass.
entries.model_notes: Temporary lesson station at a stated distance from the front door.

entries.description: An escaped Bowtruckle runs from the lesson into the Forest and disappears among the tree roots. The school bell is audible distantly across the grounds.
entries.model_notes: Small-scale roots and traversable lawn-to-Forest interface; not a mapped permanent Bowtruckle colony.

entries.location: Creature lesson to greenhouses and castle
entries.description: From Hagrid’s lesson the friends cross the vegetable patch to the greenhouses. The nearest greenhouse has a door used by the departing fourth-year class; after a lesson using dragon-dung fertiliser, pupils go back uphill to the castle.
entries.model_notes: Connects cabin lesson, vegetable patch, greenhouses and uphill castle return.

entries.description: Angelina says she has booked the pitch for Friday’s Keeper trials.
entries.model_notes: Reported scheduled use, not permanent physical exclusivity.

entries.location: Defence teacher’s office location and former states
entries.description: Umbridge’s office is on the third floor and is the office formerly occupied by Lockhart, Lupin and the impostor Moody: respectively self-portraits, dark creatures in cages or tanks, and detection instruments and artefacts.
entries.model_notes: Identifies continuity of one room despite changing decor; retain historical occupant states.

entries.location: Umbridge’s office decor and detention furniture
entries.description: Lace covers and cloths drape the surfaces. Dried-flower vases stand on doilies, and wall plates depict brightly coloured kittens with different neck bows. A cloth covers her desk; a small lace-covered table and straight-backed chair hold Harry’s detention parchment. Her desk has drawers.
entries.model_notes: September occupation state; do not retain predecessors’ equipment without evidence.

entries.description: A long thin black quill with an unusually sharp point writes with Harry’s blood without an ink supply and cuts matching words into his hand; repeated use eventually leaves lasting cuts.
entries.model_notes: Interactive office prop; effects belong to this quill, not the room’s architecture.

entries.description: Her office has a window through which darkness falls. Moving his chair about an inch to the right gives Harry a distant view of Keeper trials and three high goalposts; individual identities remain too distant to resolve. The pitch disappears from view after nightfall.
entries.model_notes: Explicit third-floor office-to-pitch sightline; no compass direction or distance in yards.

entries.description: Returning from Umbridge, Harry climbs a staircase to the seventh floor, turns right at its top and encounters Ron hiding behind a statue of Lachlan the Lanky. They continue to the Fat Lady.
entries.model_notes: Precise local floor and turn; does not fix total travel from the third floor or statue-to-portrait distance.

entries.location: Gryffindor dormitory and morning common room
entries.description: Early sunlight enters through a gap in Harry’s four-poster curtains. Below the dormitories, the common room has an extinguished grate and old squashy fireside chair; the usual evening rubbish and elf hats have been cleared overnight. Sunlight advances halfway across the room.
entries.model_notes: Cleaning observed, cleaner identity not supplied; direction of sunrise through particular windows unspecified.

entries.description: On a route from Gryffindor to the Owlery, Nick warns of a bust of Paracelsus halfway along the corridor. Harry turns left rather than right, taking a longer upward route past many windows.
entries.model_notes: Bust placement and safer route observed/reported separately: planned falling-bust prank is Nick’s report, not an observed collapse.

entries.description: Mrs Norris disappears behind a statue of Wilfred the Wistful on Harry’s longer route to the Owlery.
entries.model_notes: A distinct statue; no material or precise floor supplied.

entries.description: The circular Owlery has glassless windows, rafters supporting hundreds of owls and a vaulted ceiling whose upper reaches accommodate Hedwig. Straw, droppings and small animal bones cover the floor.
entries.model_notes: Keep vertical owl-roost space and unglazed openings.

entries.description: Owls launch through windows. The room has a handled door and stairs descending outside it; after leaving, Harry and Cho reach the entrance to a corridor leading toward the castle’s west wing.
entries.model_notes: Does not locate Ravenclaw quarters or assert that the Owlery itself is in the west wing.

entries.location: Owlery view over cabin and Forest
entries.description: From one Owlery window Hagrid’s hut is clearly visible with drawn curtains and a smokeless chimney. Beyond the swaying Forest treetops Harry sees a black leathery-winged carriage creature rise, circle and plunge back among the trees.
entries.model_notes: Cabin appears unoccupied to Harry; flight confirms Forest presence rather than an exact nest.

entries.description: Harry and Ron walk downhill over sloping lawns to the pitch. Approaching it, Harry sees the Forbidden Forest to his right and owls around the Owlery tower.
entries.model_notes: Right is relative to this approach, not a compass direction. Preserve reciprocal castle/pitch travel.

entries.description: A cupboard in the changing room stores balls. Angelina enters from the Captain’s office; players carry a ball crate onto the pitch and change back after practice.
entries.model_notes: Connect Captain’s office to changing-room circulation; no full room plan.

entries.location: Quidditch stadium goal and stand layout
entries.description: The pitch has three tall goalposts at the defended end, including left, middle and right hoops. Spectators halfway up the stands can jeer audibly across the stadium. Practice uses the opposite end and a ball crate on the ground.
entries.model_notes: Goals at opposite ends are explicit in action; no dimensions inferred.

entries.description: Fred and George fly toward the castle supporting injured Katie between them after Angelina says she needs the hospital wing.
entries.model_notes: Airborne departure is observed; actual hospital entry and route inside are not narrated.

entries.description: Pupils study at tables and armchairs beside the fire. A screech owl waits on a windowsill; Ron opens the window and it flies inside to land on his essay, then leaves. Hermione’s knitting needles work suspended in midair.
entries.model_notes: Operable common-room window and exterior owl access; no claim of window count.

entries.description: Harry kneels on a singed threadbare hearthrug before the fire. Sirius’s head appears among the flames for conversation and vanishes with a small pop; he reports checking the room briefly every hour beforehand.
entries.model_notes: Remote head communication is observed, hourly checks reported. Do not model full-body arrival from this scene.

entries.description: After using the blackboard and submitting potion flasks at Snape’s desk, pupils climb steps out of the dungeon and cross the Entrance Hall toward lunch.
entries.model_notes: Explicit upward connection from dungeon circulation to Entrance Hall.

entries.description: Harry sits at the back of the shadowed classroom. Umbridge enters through the floor trapdoor and draws an armchair to a point a few inches behind Trelawney’s seat; she later descends the silver ladder, and the pupils reach Defence ten minutes afterward.
entries.model_notes: Movable inspection chair and approximate travel interval, not a measured direct-route duration.

entries.description: Umbridge walks around the front row of student desks to address Hermione, then returns to the front of the room.
entries.model_notes: Confirms desks arranged in rows; the count and spacing are unspecified.

entries.description: Umbridge sits in a classroom corner with her clipboard. McGonagall has a teacher’s desk; a box of live mice is passed among pupils for Vanishing practice.
entries.model_notes: Inspection seating and lesson materials are temporary.

entries.description: Pupils walk down the lawns toward the Forest to a trestle table holding captive Bowtruckles searching for woodlice. Umbridge walks among the students and returns across the lawn to the castle afterward.
entries.model_notes: Repeated concrete lesson setup; planned Porlocks, Kneazles, Crups and Knarls are not confirmed installed exhibits.

entries.description: Windowpanes rattle in a night breeze and the fire gutters. Crookshanks runs under a sofa when Harry breaks a china bowl; Harry’s Reparo reassembles the bowl, leaving its spilled liquid unrecovered.
entries.model_notes: Confirms sofa with under-clearance and glazed windows; broken bowl is repaired locally in the scene.

entries.description: Filch checks a parental-permission list before pupils leave onto the stone steps. The friends descend the wide drive to the gates, pass between the winged-boar-topped stone pillars and turn left onto the village road.
entries.temporal: Late September and first October Hogsmeade weekend, 1995
entries.model_notes: Explicit gate-to-village turn; compass orientation unspecified.

entries.description: Following the main street past Zonko’s and the post office, they turn up a side street to a small inn at its top. Returning, they turn into the High Street and stop outside Scrivenshaft’s.
entries.temporal: Late September and first October Hogsmeade weekend, 1995
entries.model_notes: Village detail retained as a route to the off-main-road school meeting, not a complete village inventory.

entries.description: A battered wooden sign hangs above the door from a rusty bracket, showing a severed boar’s head bleeding onto a white cloth. Opening the door lets a band of dusty sunlight cross the bar.
entries.temporal: Late September and first October Hogsmeade weekend, 1995
entries.model_notes: Wind makes the hanging sign creak.

entries.description: The bar is one small dingy dirty room smelling of goats, with grime-encrusted bay windows admitting little daylight. Candle stubs on rough wooden tables supply light; accumulated dirt covers a stone floor.
entries.temporal: Late September and first October Hogsmeade weekend, 1995
entries.model_notes: Observed 1995 condition of the castle-boundary meeting location.

entries.description: A table stands in one window; a shadowy corner is beside the fireplace. The barman comes from a back room; bottles are stored under the counter, and an ancient wooden till opens its drawer automatically. The group takes the table farthest from the bar and adds chairs for twenty-five newcomers.
entries.temporal: Late September and first October Hogsmeade weekend, 1995
entries.model_notes: At least twenty-eight students occupy the room; retain count as event occupancy, not a code capacity.

entries.description: Hermione describes the Three Broomsticks as usually crowded and noisy and reports Flitwick confirming that pupils may enter the Hog’s Head. Harry contrasts its dirt with the Three Broomsticks’ large clean warm-looking bar.
entries.temporal: Late September and first October Hogsmeade weekend, 1995
entries.model_notes: Pub access permission is reported; no physical enforcement barrier asserted.

entries.description: Terry Boot reports seeing a sword in Dumbledore’s office and hearing one of the wall portraits tell of Harry using it to kill the Basilisk; Harry confirms the deed.
entries.temporal: Late September and first October Hogsmeade weekend, 1995
entries.model_notes: Reported office contents and talking wall portrait; this does not newly describe the sword’s display case.

entries.description: Katie suggests the library, Dean an unused classroom, and Ron recalls McGonagall permitting use of her room for Harry’s Triwizard practice. No meeting room is selected here.
entries.temporal: Late September and first October Hogsmeade weekend, 1995
entries.model_notes: Separate proposed venues from confirmed use; Ron’s past-use recollection is reported.

entries.description: The friends study in the shade of a large beech on the lake edge during the last autumn sunshine.
entries.temporal: Early October 1995, after first Hogsmeade meeting
entries.model_notes: A specific lakeshore tree and usable shaded ground; no precise compass position.

entries.description: A large decree covers the common-room board’s secondhand-book lists, school rules, training timetable, Chocolate Frog trades, joke-test recruitment, Hogsmeade dates and lost-and-found notices.
entries.temporal: Early October 1995, after first Hogsmeade meeting
entries.model_notes: October notice state; decree disbands groups of three or more until approved.

entries.description: Behind the girls’ door a spiral staircase transforms when Ron reaches its sixth step: a klaxon sounds and the steps merge into a long smooth spiralling stone slide, delivering him to the common room. Girls, including Hermione, slide down onto a rug.
entries.temporal: Early October 1995, after first Hogsmeade meeting
entries.model_notes: Observed access prevention for Ron. Hermione’s explanation that founders distrusted boys and that girls can enter boys’ rooms is reported; no reset timing shown.

entries.description: Binns floats an inch above his chair. The classroom has rows of seats and a narrow external window ledge, thick window glass and a sliding catch; Harry opens it to admit injured Hedwig.
entries.temporal: Early October 1995, after first Hogsmeade meeting
entries.model_notes: Operable classroom window; small ledge need not be a human route.

entries.description: Harry leaves History of Magic, follows its corridor past a window overlooking the grounds near Hagrid’s cabin, then goes downstairs to the staff room.
entries.temporal: Early October 1995, after first Hogsmeade meeting
entries.model_notes: The classroom is above the staff-room approach, without an exact floor difference.

entries.description: Two stone gargoyles flank the staff-room door and speak to Harry. Teachers open the door from inside; at break the adjacent corridor carries students in both directions and leads out into a courtyard with a sheltered corner.
entries.temporal: Early October 1995, after first Hogsmeade meeting
entries.model_notes: Talking guards do not demonstrate a password or physically blocked entry.

entries.description: Grubbly-Plank says Hagrid has trained the Hogwarts Thestrals not to attack owls, although Thestrals can prey on birds.
entries.temporal: Early October 1995, after first Hogsmeade meeting
entries.model_notes: Reported local animal-management constraint; Hedwig’s actual attacker remains unproven.

entries.description: After courtyard break the friends descend stone steps to the dungeons; at the bottom they reach the queue outside Snape’s classroom door.
entries.temporal: Early October 1995, after first Hogsmeade meeting
entries.model_notes: Retain bottom-of-stairs classroom relationship without importing an exact floor count.

entries.location: Potions classroom rows and inspection corner
entries.description: Snape’s classroom has two lines of desks with circulation between them and a dim corner occupied by Umbridge. Potion mixtures remain from the preceding lesson over the weekend; instructions appear on the board.
entries.temporal: Early October 1995, after first Hogsmeade meeting
entries.model_notes: Not proof of exactly two desk rows in the whole room; describes the lines she walks between.

entries.description: The Divination room is hot and heavily perfumed, with student pouffes and a high-backed teacher’s chair.
entries.temporal: Early October 1995, after first Hogsmeade meeting
entries.model_notes: Adds teacher-chair form to repeated classroom atmosphere.

entries.description: The twins demonstrate vomiting sweets into a bucket, whose contents Lee magically vanishes. Later the friends kneel on the hearthrug, which has a hole; the fireplace has a solid brick side wall and hot flames.
entries.temporal: Early October 1995, after first Hogsmeade meeting
entries.model_notes: Temporary demonstration equipment; the wall and worn rug are permanent fittings.

entries.description: Sirius recalls a roomy secret passage behind a large fourth-floor mirror, potentially wide enough for jinx practice. Harry reports the twins saying it is now blocked by a cave-in or similar collapse.
entries.temporal: Early October 1995, after first Hogsmeade meeting
entries.model_notes: Historical capacity and present blockage are reports; collapse wording is uncertain, and no destination is given.

entries.description: Sirius disappears from the common-room fire as Umbridge’s ringed hand appears and gropes through the flames. Harry can still see the hand from the boys’ dormitory doorway while the friends flee.
entries.temporal: Early October 1995, after first Hogsmeade meeting
entries.model_notes: Demonstrates remote reaching and doorway-to-hearth sightline, not a secret physical tunnel.

entries.description: Sirius proposes the Shrieking Shack for lessons; Hermione contrasts four past animal-form users with twenty-eight current pupils who could not all be concealed by one cloak.
entries.temporal: Early October 1995, after first Hogsmeade meeting
entries.model_notes: A rejected access/concealment proposal, not an actual journey or measured shack capacity.

entries.description: Bullfrogs and ravens occupy classroom desks during Silencing practice; heavy rain pounds the windows.
entries.temporal: October 1995, first DA meeting and preceding storm
entries.model_notes: Temporary living practice materials and weather.

entries.description: Rain keeps pupils indoors for break in an overcrowded first-floor classroom with seats, windows and a chandelier near which Peeves floats while firing ink pellets.
entries.temporal: October 1995, first DA meeting and preceding storm
entries.model_notes: An unnamed room, distinct from an assumed identity with Charms.

entries.description: The changing rooms are warm and lit, with a roof audibly struck by rain, a window, benches and cloak pegs. Angelina emerges from the Captain’s office.
entries.temporal: October 1995, first DA meeting and preceding storm
entries.model_notes: Building is exposed to wind and rain; no material of roof stated.

entries.description: Grass on the approach is sodden and slippery, the pitch centre deepens into mud, and fading light, wind and sweeping rain severely restrict visibility. Rain beating the lake can be heard from the pitch. Players return uphill over muddy lawns.
entries.temporal: October 1995, first DA meeting and preceding storm
entries.model_notes: October storm state; Impervius improves rain shedding without restoring useful visibility.

entries.description: After midnight the common-room candles are all extinguished and its fire is almost out. Dobby returns Hedwig beside the hat-covered table and says other elves now refuse to clean Gryffindor Tower because hidden clothing insults them, so he does all its cleaning.
entries.temporal: October 1995, first DA meeting and preceding storm
entries.model_notes: Dark room observed; exclusive cleaning arrangement is Dobby’s report, not proof any elf has been freed.

entries.description: Dobby calls it the Come and Go Room or Room of Requirement: it can be entered by a person with real need, appears intermittently, and supplies what that seeker needs. He says few know it and many accidental users cannot find it again.
entries.temporal: October 1995, first DA meeting and preceding storm
entries.model_notes: Reported rules here; later observed entrance is separately recorded.

entries.description: Dobby reports an elf-sized bed and Butterbeer antidotes when sheltering drunken Winky, and extra cleaning supplies for Filch. Harry recalls Dumbledore’s chamber-pot room and proposes that it is the same place; Dobby expects it could be.
entries.temporal: October 1995, first DA meeting and preceding storm
entries.model_notes: Bed and supplies are reported; identification of the chamber-pot room is a character inference rather than independently confirmed identity.

entries.description: Pupils splash across a flooded vegetable patch to Herbology while rain hammers the greenhouse roof. Creature lessons are moved from the exposed grounds to a free classroom on the ground floor; evening Quidditch is cancelled.
entries.temporal: October 1995, first DA meeting and preceding storm
entries.model_notes: Ground-floor room is unnamed; do not assign it other classes’ identity.

entries.description: The meeting place is on the seventh floor opposite the tapestry of Barnabas the Barmy trying to teach trolls ballet. The friends leave Gryffindor, reach the top of a final staircase and follow the corridor to a blank wall facing the enormous moving tapestry.
entries.temporal: October 1995, first DA meeting and preceding storm
entries.model_notes: Fifth-years may use corridors until nine; staircase sequence supplies no exact common-room level change.

entries.description: They pass the blank wall three times concentrating on a concealed practice place, turning at a window just beyond it and a man-sized vase on its other side. A highly polished door with a brass handle appears after the third pass.
entries.temporal: October 1995, first DA meeting and preceding storm
entries.model_notes: Window and vase bound the walking segment; no measured separation.

entries.description: The door opens into a spacious room lit with flickering torches like those in the dungeons eight floors below.
entries.temporal: October 1995, first DA meeting and preceding storm
entries.model_notes: Eight-floor relation is textual; avoid deriving ceiling heights or a global building grid.

entries.description: Wooden bookcases line the walls with hundreds of large leather-bound defence books. Large silk cushions replace chairs on the floor and allow all twenty-eight participants to sit.
entries.temporal: October 1995, first DA meeting and preceding storm
entries.model_notes: State supplied for this meeting, not a permanent layout across requirements.

entries.description: Far-end shelves hold Sneakoscopes, Secrecy Sensors and a large cracked Foe-Glass with moving indistinct figures. Harry recognises the glass as apparently the one from impostor Moody’s office. The entrance has a key protruding from a working lock.
entries.temporal: October 1995, first DA meeting and preceding storm
entries.model_notes: Recognition is Harry’s belief, not proven transfer of the same object; detectors can be fooled according to Harry.

entries.description: Fred recalls that he and George once hid from Filch in this room when it was a broom cupboard.
entries.temporal: October 1995, first DA meeting and preceding storm
entries.model_notes: Reported previous manifestation; not an extra simultaneously accessible room.

entries.location: DA wall notice and practice clearances
entries.description: Hermione pins the signed Dumbledore’s Army parchment on the wall. Paired duelling leaves room for Harry to circulate, sends books off shelves and a wand against the ceiling; Harry finds a whistle atop books immediately after needing one.
entries.temporal: October 1995, first DA meeting and preceding storm
entries.model_notes: Local movement and conjured/provided prop, without invented dimensions or lasting structural damage.

entries.description: The Marauder’s Map shows Hufflepuffs returning to the basement corridor that also leads to the kitchens, Ravenclaws to a tower on the west side, and Gryffindors along the corridor to the Fat Lady.
entries.temporal: October 1995, first DA meeting and preceding storm
entries.model_notes: Narrated observation through the map; no complete Hufflepuff entrance or Ravenclaw interior supplied.

entries.description: After the final three pupils leave, the door melts back into stone behind them.
entries.temporal: October 1995, first DA meeting and preceding storm
entries.model_notes: Observed closure effect; does not prove the contents cease to exist.

entries.location: Room of Requirement detector table damage
entries.description: During later DA practice Parvati’s Reductor Curse reduces the table carrying the Sneakoscopes to dust.
entries.temporal: Late October to first November Quidditch match, 1995
entries.model_notes: A table is present in this later manifestation; do not silently substitute the earlier detector shelves. Repair is not described.

entries.description: Hermione distributes fake Galleons from a basket. Their edge numbers communicate meeting dates and times through a Protean Charm and grow hot when changed.
entries.temporal: Late October to first November Quidditch match, 1995
entries.model_notes: Portable props for meeting coordination; not fixed geometry.

entries.description: McGonagall says she is accustomed to keeping the Quidditch Cup in her study.
entries.temporal: Late October to first November Quidditch match, 1995
entries.model_notes: Reported trophy location, without a display stand or case.

entries.description: Snape books the pitch repeatedly for Slytherin practices, restricting Gryffindor access. Fourteen witnesses report Alicia being jinxed from behind while working in the library; she attends the hospital wing.
entries.temporal: Late October to first November Quidditch match, 1995
entries.model_notes: Pitch access is scheduled, not fenced by House. Library attack is a reported incident, with no asserted furniture damage.

entries.description: Hard morning frosts and icy draughts follow October storms. Surrounding mountains are snowcapped, the sky and Great Hall ceiling pale pearly grey, and castle corridors become cold enough for dragonskin gloves.
entries.temporal: Late October to first November Quidditch match, 1995
entries.model_notes: Seasonal thermal and distant-terrain state.

entries.description: From the Hall the players cross the Entrance Hall, descend stone steps and follow frost-crunching sloping lawns down to the stadium and changing rooms.
entries.temporal: Late October to first November Quidditch match, 1995
entries.model_notes: Repeated route with frozen ground; calm overcast conditions improve visibility.

entries.description: Banked benches in spectator stands receive hundreds of spectators. Players file from the changing room onto the pitch; supporters occupy identifiable Slytherin and Gryffindor sections, with Pansy at the front of the Slytherin stands.
entries.temporal: Late October to first November Quidditch match, 1995
entries.model_notes: Sound carries throughout stadium. Three goalhoops at each defended end; no precise audience capacity or compass placement.

entries.location: Frozen pitch and low flight space
entries.description: The Snitch flies near the foot of a goalpost toward the other side of the stands. Harry catches it only feet above the surface and falls five or six feet onto the frozen pitch after a Bludger strike.
entries.temporal: Late October to first November Quidditch match, 1995
entries.model_notes: Specific local flight and fall clearances, not goalpost height.

entries.description: After the fight Harry and George walk from the pitch uphill to the castle, through a quiet Entrance Hall, then along a corridor to McGonagall’s office; she approaches behind them.
entries.temporal: Late October to first November Quidditch match, 1995
entries.model_notes: Intervening floors and stairs are not described.

entries.description: McGonagall’s tartan biscuit tin slides off her desk and bursts open on the floor, scattering Ginger Newts; she has thrown her scarf onto the floor.
entries.temporal: Late October to first November Quidditch match, 1995
entries.model_notes: Temporary movable clutter; no permanent office damage.

entries.description: Umbridge announces that Harry’s, Fred’s and George’s brooms will be confiscated and kept in her office after their lifetime Quidditch bans.
entries.temporal: Late October to first November Quidditch match, 1995
entries.model_notes: Announced storage plan rather than a narrated transfer in this chapter.

entries.description: Snow swirls against the dark common-room window; Hermione sees enough outside to announce Hagrid’s return. The captured Snitch flies around the room as Crookshanks leaps between chairs pursuing it.
entries.temporal: Late October to first November Quidditch match, 1995
entries.model_notes: Return signal is not specified here; do not invent a lamp sighting until described.

entries.description: The friends descend many staircases from the portrait hole, cross the Entrance Hall and enter snowy grounds. Hagrid’s windows show little golden squares and smoke rises from his chimney as they approach his wooden front door.
entries.temporal: Snowy November night of Hagrid’s return, 1995
entries.model_notes: Front door has a keyhole and bolt; snow tracks reveal travel despite the Invisibility Cloak.

entries.description: Hagrid closes curtains after admitting them. A travelling cloak lies over a chair and a large haversack against the wall just inside the door. He heats a copper kettle over the fire and serves tea in bucket-shaped mugs.
entries.temporal: Snowy November night of Hagrid’s return, 1995
entries.model_notes: Travel equipment marks recent return; curtains and fire are fittings.

entries.description: An enormous wooden table stands in the cabin centre. A tea towel initially covers a raw dragon steak slightly larger than a car tyre; Hagrid uses it as a cold dressing and it later falls to the floor.
entries.temporal: Snowy November night of Hagrid’s return, 1995
entries.model_notes: Temporary medical/food prop and mess on central work surface.

entries.location: Cabin door window and dog basket
entries.description: A thin-curtained window beside the doorway shows Umbridge’s shadow before entry. The friends hide in a corner, while Hagrid conceals two mugs beneath the cushion in Fang’s basket; Hermione’s broken mug remains on the floor.
entries.temporal: Snowy November night of Hagrid’s return, 1995
entries.model_notes: Preserve door-adjacent window, dog basket and temporary china fragments.

entries.description: Umbridge walks the length of the cabin, looks beneath the bed and inside cupboards and Hagrid’s enormous cooking cauldron, passing within two inches of the hidden pupils against a wall. The vast bed occupies a corner.
entries.temporal: Snowy November night of Hagrid’s return, 1995
entries.model_notes: Under-bed clearance and walkable perimeter observed; no numeric cabin dimensions.

entries.description: Hagrid parts a curtain about an inch to watch Umbridge returning to the castle. She has reported three sets of footprints from the castle doors with none returning; the friends later go uphill through thicker snow, erasing their tracks with Hermione’s Obliteration Charm.
entries.temporal: Snowy November night of Hagrid’s return, 1995
entries.model_notes: Initial footprint count is Umbridge’s report; later physical erasure is observed. No cloak-based footprint immunity.

entries.description: Hagrid says he has raised special lesson creatures for years and believes his is Britain’s only domestic herd.
entries.temporal: Snowy November night of Hagrid’s return, 1995
entries.model_notes: Reported still-unnamed herd; location and species await the next lesson.

entries.description: Two feet of snow cover the grounds; students skate on the frozen lake, toboggan and enchant snowballs to fly up and hit Gryffindor Tower windows. Ron opens a common-room window and is struck by a snowball before shutting it.
entries.model_notes: November freeze and student use, not year-round lake solidity.

entries.description: Hermione says she waits at Hagrid’s door for half an hour before he emerges from the Forest.
entries.model_notes: Does not confirm a Chimaera: Hermione explicitly doubts he has one.

entries.description: Pupils run up the aisle between Gryffindor and Hufflepuff tables to greet Hagrid at the staff table.
entries.model_notes: Repeated adjacency and aisle-to-staff-table connection.

entries.description: Hagrid waits at the Forest edge carrying half a dead cow, then leads pupils into dark trees for about ten minutes to a dense stand where the light resembles twilight and no snow reaches the ground.
entries.model_notes: Sheltered snowy-season route; no compass direction or measured distance.

entries.description: Hagrid lays the carcass on the ground and gives shrieking calls. Thestrals emerge among the trees, one from between two gnarled yews, and eat with pointed fangs; more arrive with leathery wings folded and long black tails swishing.
entries.model_notes: Actual Forest feeding site, distinct from the coach road.

entries.description: Hagrid identifies a resident Forest herd founded with one male and five females; Tenebrus was the first born there. He says the herd mainly pulls school coaches, sometimes carrying Dumbledore on journeys, and tame animals have an exceptional sense of direction.
entries.model_notes: Reported husbandry and abilities; not a census of the current herd.

entries.description: Hermione states, and Hagrid confirms, that people who have seen death can see Thestrals. Harry, Neville and one Slytherin see the feeding animals while others see flesh disappear.
entries.model_notes: Rule is reported and classroom visibility difference directly observed. Do not infer that Umbridge sees them from her mere arrival.

entries.description: Pupils return uphill toward the castle along channels previously made through snow. Hermione melts an easier route through untouched snow between the class and the greenhouses using hot air from her wand.
entries.model_notes: Retain travel sequence without straight-line assumptions.

entries.description: Further snow and bitter cold keep younger pupils indoors during breaks. Prefects supervise castle decorations including tinsel and patrol corridors with Filch.
entries.model_notes: Tinsel difficulty is Ron’s report; no specific decorated room supplied.

entries.description: Torches flare when Harry enters. A hundred golden Harry-faced Christmas baubles hang from the ceiling until he removes them; a large clump of mistletoe with white berries remains overhead.
entries.model_notes: Harry attributes decorations to Dobby; actual baubles and mistletoe observed. Nargles are Luna’s unsupported claim.

entries.description: Cushions are laid across the floor for Stunning practice, but the room is too confined for everyone to practise simultaneously; half observe while half cast, then swap. Cushions are stacked afterward and pupils depart in twos and threes.
entries.model_notes: Concrete capacity constraint despite the room’s spacious appearance; no metric size.

entries.description: The friends work beside the fire at a table and armchairs; Ron lies on the hearthrug and knocks his ink bottle over it when sitting up.
entries.model_notes: Ink spill is temporary; no subsequent rug cleaning described.

entries.location: Boys’ dormitory window and bed relation
entries.description: With his bed hangings open, Harry sees stars through a window beside Neville’s bed. His glasses rest on his bedside table and Ron speaks from his right; McGonagall later reaches the dormitory via the stairs.
entries.model_notes: Right is from Harry’s position in bed; the subsequent snake-vision corridor is not Hogwarts.

entries.description: McGonagall leads Harry and Ron down the dormitory spiral stairs, across the common room and through the portrait hole along the Fat Lady’s moonlit corridor. After a few minutes they reach the office’s stone gargoyle.
entries.temporal: December 1995, night of Arthur Weasley’s attack and following day
entries.model_notes: Travel duration approximate; intervening corridor turns and floors not supplied.

entries.description: Fizzing Whizzbee makes the gargoyle leap aside and the wall split, exposing continuously ascending stone spiral stairs. The wall closes behind riders; tight circles bring them to a polished oak door with a brass griffin-shaped knocker. The door opens of itself after three knocks.
entries.temporal: December 1995, night of Arthur Weasley’s attack and following day
entries.model_notes: Password belongs to December 1995.

entries.description: Tables hold fragile silver instruments, unusually still and smokeless tonight; former heads’ portraits cover the walls. Fawkes sleeps on a perch beside and behind the entrance door. A candle lights papers on Dumbledore’s desk, behind which stands his high-backed chair.
entries.temporal: December 1995, night of Arthur Weasley’s attack and following day
entries.model_notes: Fawkes perch position explicit; instrument activity varies with time.

entries.description: Everard’s portrait hangs near the ceiling beside Dilys’s; after they leave their frames, one shows a dark curtain and the other a leather armchair. They return with reports from other institutions. Dumbledore explains they travel among their own portraits; Hogwarts subjects usually enter neighbouring pictures.
entries.temporal: December 1995, night of Arthur Weasley’s attack and following day
entries.model_notes: Remote institutional connection, not a physical passage. Everard returns at the top of the wall to the visitors’ right.

entries.description: McGonagall conjures three straight-backed wooden chairs for herself, Harry and Ron.
entries.temporal: December 1995, night of Arthur Weasley’s attack and following day
entries.model_notes: Event furniture, distinct from Dumbledore’s comfortable chintz chairs at the Ministry.

entries.description: Dumbledore places a silver instrument from its spindly table onto his desk and activates it by wand. A tiny top tube emits pale-green smoke forming a serpent that divides into two; a second tap stops it and the smoke vanishes.
entries.temporal: December 1995, night of Arthur Weasley’s attack and following day
entries.model_notes: Function remains unexplained; do not label it a confirmed truth detector.

entries.description: A portrait of pointed-bearded Phineas in Slytherin green and silver hangs in the office with a Slytherin banner backdrop. He moves to his other portrait in Harry’s Grimmauld Place bedroom to deliver a message, then returns.
entries.temporal: December 1995, night of Arthur Weasley’s attack and following day
entries.model_notes: Specific remote portrait connection observed through departures/return and Dumbledore’s explanation; Armando Dippet also has an office portrait.

entries.description: A cupboard behind Harry and Ron contains a blackened old kettle. Dumbledore enchants it blue momentarily with Portus; five pupils touch it at his desk and are transported to Grimmauld Place’s basement kitchen.
entries.temporal: December 1995, night of Arthur Weasley’s attack and following day
entries.model_notes: Demonstrated authorised Portkey departure inside Hogwarts, distinct from unsafe watched Floo travel; no general permission for all Portkeys inferred.

entries.description: Fawkes disappears in a flash of fire; later flame appears in mid-office leaving one golden feather as a warning of an approaching visitor.
entries.temporal: December 1995, night of Arthur Weasley’s attack and following day
entries.model_notes: Remote phoenix warning transport, not an architectural passage.

entries.description: The hospital reception contains a second portrait of Dilys Derwent with silver ringlets, labelled Hogwarts headmistress 1741–1768; she notices Harry’s group and leaves her frame.
entries.temporal: December 1995, night of Arthur Weasley’s attack and following day
entries.model_notes: Only the school-linked portrait network is catalogued from this remote hospital; unrelated ward architecture excluded.

entries.description: Hermione cites Hogwarts: A History to state that nobody can Apparate or Disapparate within Hogwarts, rejecting Harry’s idea that he was physically transported out of his dormitory during the snake vision. Ron says he remained in bed.
entries.model_notes: Reported general restriction and eyewitness denial of that journey; do not conflate it with the separately observed authorised Portkey departure.
